properties.address: 13 E Basin Dr SW, Washington, DC 20004, USA

properties.foundation_analysis: The subterranean profile beneath the southern shore of the Tidal Basin consists of anthropogenic hydraulic silt and gravel infill over late Quaternary Potomac Formation alluvium. Deep crystalline metamorphic bedrock (Piedmont schist/gneiss) lies tens of meters below. The memorial foundation rests on heavy reinforced concrete caissons sunk through the mud into solid bedrock to counteract structural settlement. Above grade, the monument's exterior peristyle, stylobate, steps, and drum are constructed from fine-grained white Imperial Danby marble quarried from Dorset Mountain in Vermont (Ordovician Shelburne Formation). The shallow stepped dome is faced in Middle Mississippian Indiana oolitic limestone (Salem Formation). The circular interior colonnade features Georgia white marble, with floor and substructure elements anchored by pink granite from Salisbury, North Carolina. Non-staining Portland cement mortar with lime binder fills the stone masonry joints.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: The memorial is surrounded by dense groves of mature Yoshino cherry trees (*Prunus × yedoensis*) and Kwanzan cherries (*Prunus serrulata*) exhibiting full, textured summer canopies of deep green foliage and dark gnarled bark. Flanking the lawns and pathways are mature native hardwoods including American elm (*Ulmus americana*), willow oak (*Quercus phellos*), sweetgum (*Liquidambar styraciflua*), and red maple (*Acer rubrum*). The background shoreline across the Tidal Basin is densely populated with broadleaf deciduous tree cover.

properties.architectural_summary: Designed by John Russell Pope, Daniel P. Higgins, and Otto R. Eggers in the Neoclassical / Beaux-Arts Pantheon-inspired typology, completed in 1943. The primary structure comprises a monumental circular peristyle colonnade of 26 fluted Ionic columns supporting an unadorned frieze and a stepped circular attic topped by a shallow hemispherical dome. A pedimented portico opens north toward the National Mall, framed by a broad cascading flight of granite and marble steps leading down to the water's edge. The circular drum features rhythmic vertical openings between columns into an open-air central rotunda. Behind the water body across the axis rises the vertical obelisk of the Washington Monument (Robert Mills, 1884), perfectly plumbed to true gravity vertical against the distant planar geometry of Federal Triangle office complexes.
